In 1971, a seventeen year old girl fell three kilometres from the sky, and lived.
On Christmas Eve, Juliane Koepcke and her mother boarded a flight over the Peruvian rainforest.
Halfway there, the plane flew into a huge thunderstorm.
Lightning hit the plane, and it broke apart in the air.
Juliane was still strapped into her row of seats, falling through the sky.
She crashed through the trees and woke up the next day on the jungle floor.
She had a broken collarbone, a deep cut on her arm, and only one shoe.
Her father had once taught her a simple rule. If you are lost, find water and follow it downstream. It leads to people.
So she found a small stream, and she followed it.
For eleven days she waded through the river, past crocodiles and piranhas.
Then she found a hut and a boat. A few hours later, loggers found her.
Ninety one people died in that crash. Juliane was the only survivor, and she later became a rainforest scientist.
